product: BricsCAD Ultimate (Bricsys, a Hexagon company; official site now bricscad.octave.com)
version: V27 (launch keynote 20 October 2026; Windows release notes already at build 27.1.05) from Octave, the company Bricsys became in 2026 as a Hexagon spin-off. The inventory below was researched against V26 (October 2025, V26.2 March 2026) and marks V27 additions where known; V27 pricing was not re-checked (editor's own search, 2026-10-21)
summary: BricsCAD V26 is an AutoCAD-compatible DWG CAD sold in five inheriting editions (Lite 2D; Pro 2D/3D incl. civil and point clouds; Mechanical and BIM on top of Pro; Ultimate = all). Perpetual licences are still sold from the official store (Ultimate EUR 2,640 one-time incl. first-year maintenance, renewal EUR 440/yr, optional from year two); the US perpetual price could not be captured. It runs on Windows, Linux (x86-64) and macOS (Rosetta 2, no native Apple-silicon build yet). V26 adds 2D dynamic-block authoring, 3D solid grips, property-based selection, point-cloud linear feature detection into civil strings/surfaces, IFC 4x3, Teamcenter/Vault/ProjectWise/ACC integrations and a chat assistant (BricsCAD Assist). Civil tools (Pro+) cover TIN surfaces, grading/cut-fill balance, horizontal and vertical alignments and corridors but not parcels, pipe networks, plan production or stormwater analysis. Research caveat: only six web searches succeeded and no page could be fetched directly, so rows marked unverified need confirmation.

platforms: Windows 10 and 11, x86-64 only (Microsoft ended Windows 10 support 2025-10-14)
Linux x86-64: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer supported releases; openSUSE/Fedora builds after April 2022 with glibc >= 2.35; 3D acceleration unsupported on Intel graphics and dual-GPU laptops
macOS 12 Monterey or later; runs on Apple silicon through Rosetta 2 (since V21.2.06); native Apple-silicon build planned, not shipped
Hardware: Core i5/Ryzen 5 min (i7/i9, Ryzen 7/9 recommended); 8 GB RAM min, 16 GB recommended; 3 GB disk for Ultimate
No ARM, web or mobile build

unique_strengths: Perpetual licence still sold from the official store (Ultimate EUR 2,640) with maintenance optional after year one, unlike Autodesk's subscription-only model
One DWG platform spanning 2D, 3D direct modelling, sheet metal, BIM and civil (Ultimate) on Windows, Linux and macOS
AutoCAD-compatible automation surface: LISP in all editions, BRX/.NET/COM in Pro+ (unverified edition split), easing migration of LISP libraries
Local, non-cloud machine learning (predictive Quad) and deterministic productivity tools (Blockify, Auto-Parametrize) that do not depend on vendor servers
V26 enterprise integrations (Teamcenter, Vault, ProjectWise, ACC) and point-cloud extraction into civil strings/surfaces
Commercial DWG CAD with a supported Linux build
notable_weaknesses: Civil tools are preliminary/site-design level: no parcels, pipe/pressure networks, plan production, survey database, quantity takeoff or stormwater analysis found
macOS build is Rosetta-emulated with no native Apple-silicon build; Linux 3D acceleration unsupported on Intel GPUs and dual-GPU laptops
User reports of V26 crashes and slowdowns on macOS and Linux
US perpetual price for Ultimate not discoverable in this session; reseller USD maintenance figures disagree (USD 441 vs 484)
'AI' branding contested: reviewer describes Blockify/Auto-Parametrize as deterministic pattern matching, not neural inference
Forum complaint about a new upgrade-and-support policy for perpetual holders (content unverified)
Dynamic-block authoring only arrived in V26; data-link support unknown
